verdict.summary: Round 1's major finding is resolved. `client_accepts_trailers` now parses q parameters case-insensitively, accepts only well-formed strictly positive qvalues, and conservatively rejects zero or malformed qvalues. The focused negotiation test covers q=0 spellings, whitespace and list positions, malformed values, and positive controls. The truncation state machine still preserves the load-bearing invariant by withholding the JSON-closing chunk until `Done`, dropping it on failure or worker disappearance, and using either a negotiated trailer or a body-frame error. The real-router and real-socket tests exercise genuine mid-stream truncation and include an uncapped anti-vacuity control. No new correctness, soundness, test-validity, security, or instruction-injection issue is evident in the diff.
